reader_notes.text: Or his angel. The Greek can refer to a human messenger or an angelic being; it does not name the messenger.
Some Greek witnesses, including Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus, read mercy rather than oil. Which reading is earlier remains uncertain.

review.mode: One bounded report-aware critique of frozen candidate, baseline and actual controls
review.outcome: No blocking defect; narrow disclosure candidate defensible
review.actual_checks: Candidate preservation/archive, all six acquired controls/pins, saved Sinaiticus complete poem/local tags and native Swete control
review.strongest_countercase: Mercy could precede contextual oil normalization; related Hebrew oil does not decide Greek priority

preflight.override: Exact target Path.read_text substitution in normal apocrypha file walk

application.action: Frozen full-record candidate installed through apply_patch after preflight and one bounded critique

serialization: Export digest: UTF-8 json.dumps(book, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')). Historical whole-book digests identify this actual pre/postflight; future checks substitute only the frozen target in then-current export.
scope: Source-variant/messenger disclosure and connected rationale only; no earliest Greek, new ink, whole-verse optimality or canon decision
